skill.name: when-analyzing-skill-gaps-use-skill-gap-analyzer
skill.description: Analyze a skill library to find coverage gaps, redundant skills, optimization opportunities, and prioritized portfolio improvements.
skill.summary: Find skill portfolio gaps, overlaps, and improvement priorities.
skill.author: DNYoussef

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives from Markdown fences, inline backticks, JSON examples, or JavaScript template literals. The real risks are workflow instructions that run npx claude-flow@alpha hooks or memory commands, which can execute external package code and write or disclose task metadata. No prompt injection attempt or deliberate data-exfiltration intent was found in the reviewed files.

remediation.issue: Workflow examples invoke npx claude-flow@alpha from skill instructions.
remediation.suggestion: Pin the package to a reviewed version, document the command purpose, and require explicit user approval before execution.

remediation.issue: The inventory command scans ~/.claude/skills by default.
remediation.suggestion: Ask the user to confirm the skill directory or provide a project-local path before scanning home-directory skill metadata.

remediation.issue: Runnable examples and pseudocode are mixed with Markdown report templates.
remediation.suggestion: Label optional commands clearly and separate non-executable examples from commands an agent may run.

content.value_statement: Skill libraries become hard to govern as coverage, overlap, and usage drift. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through structured portfolio analysis.
actual_capabilities: Builds an inventory of skills by category, capability, tag, agent, and complexity.
Compares skill capabilities against domain requirements to identify missing coverage.
Detects redundant skills using capability overlap and consolidation thresholds.
Highlights under-used and over-complex skills from usage and success metrics.
Generates prioritized recommendations for new skills, refactors, consolidation, and archival.
Defines report formats for coverage, redundancy, optimization, and scenario readiness.
limitations: Requires access to skill metadata or a skill directory supplied by the user.
Quality depends on accurate descriptions, tags, usage metrics, and success metrics.
Does not implement changes to skills without separate user action.
Example workflow uses external claude-flow commands that should be reviewed before execution.

use_cases.title: Plan a New Skill Library
use_cases.description: Map required domains, identify missing capabilities, and prioritize the first skills to create.

use_cases.title: Run a Quarterly Portfolio Review
use_cases.description: Measure coverage, redundancy, utilization, and complexity before planning maintenance work.

use_cases.title: Prepare a Refactoring Roadmap
use_cases.description: Find overlapping or over-complex skills and turn them into measurable consolidation tasks.

prompt_templates.title: Basic Gap Review
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner review of a small skill set
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze my skill library for missing coverage, duplicate capabilities, and the top three improvement priorities.

prompt_templates.title: Domain Coverage Audit
prompt_templates.scenario: Focused review by business or engineering domain
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this skill library against development, DevOps, data, AI, and integration domains. Rank gaps by priority and explain the impact.

prompt_templates.title: Redundancy and Refactor Plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Identify skills with overlapping capabilities, estimate consolidation value, and propose a phased refactor plan with risks and expected savings.

prompt_templates.title: Portfolio Optimization Report
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced review using metrics and scenario coverage
prompt_templates.prompt: Use skill metadata, usage metrics, success rates, and core scenarios to create a portfolio optimization report with immediate, monthly, and quarterly actions.

output_examples.input: A library has 47 skills across development, GitHub automation, testing, optimization, and meta tools.
output_examples.output: The report identifies low data engineering coverage, four overlapping code review skills, and one over-complex architecture skill. It recommends one new skill, one consolidation project, and one refactor.

output_examples.input: A team wants to decide which skills to maintain before a quarterly planning cycle.
output: Coverage gaps are grouped by domain and priority.
Redundant skills are listed with consolidation targets.
Short-term and long-term actions are ranked by impact and effort.

output_examples.input: A maintainer provides usage frequency, last-used dates, and average token counts.
output_examples.output: The analysis flags skills with low usage, high token cost, and low success rate. It suggests archive, promote, split, or simplify actions.

best_practices: Provide current skill metadata, usage metrics, and success metrics before requesting recommendations.
Review command examples before allowing any external tool execution.
Validate recommendations with maintainers before creating, merging, or archiving skills.
anti_patterns: Do not treat generated priorities as final decisions without human review.
Do not scan private skill directories unless the user has approved the scope.
Do not optimize only for token savings when coverage or reliability would decrease.

faq.question: What does this skill analyze?
faq.answer: It analyzes skill coverage, redundancy, utilization, complexity, scenario readiness, and improvement priorities.

faq.question: Does it create new skills automatically?
faq.answer: No. It recommends new skills or refactors, but implementation requires a separate user decision.

faq.question: Can it work with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The marketplace metadata lists Claude, Codex, and Claude Code as supported tools.

faq.question: What inputs improve the analysis?
faq.answer: Skill descriptions, tags, categories, agents, complexity, usage frequency, success rates, and token metrics improve results.

faq.question: Why does the audit mention command risk?
faq.answer: The source includes example npx commands. Users should review and approve those commands before execution.

faq.question: Is private skill data sent elsewhere?
faq.answer: No evidence found of deliberate exfiltration, but external workflow commands should be disabled or reviewed if privacy is required.
